meta: Aqua NYC spent $1,876 for 74 schedules, about $25 each, right on the good-band line and up from 72 schedules the week before.
Hutong Miami spent $1,845 for 23 schedules, about $80 each, well into the poor band and down from 32 schedules.
Hutong NYC spent $1,018 for 13 schedules, about $78 each, also in the poor band and down from 22. Meta efficiency at both Hutongs is the clearest cost problem in the market.
google: Aqua NYC Google ran $692 for about 27 booking conversions at roughly $26 CPA, just outside the good band.
Hutong NYC spent $1,245 for about 20 conversions at roughly $62 CPA, and Hutong Miami $610 for 13 at roughly $47. Both are above the $30 poor threshold.
Google conversions fell week on week at both Hutongs (NYC 31 to 20, Miami 21 to 13). Some of that is late attribution that has not settled yet.
ga4: Aqua NYC booked 215 (+3.9% WoW, -35.6% YoY) on users up 21.5% YoY. Conversion is 3.6% against 6.9% last year, so this is a conversion gap on healthy traffic.
Hutong NYC booked 136 (-3.5% WoW, -26.9% YoY) with users -27.0% YoY, so its gap is traffic-side and tracks the Google Reserve to OpenTable handoff.
Hutong Miami booked 80 (-28.6% WoW, -22.3% YoY) on users roughly flat YoY, so its conversion rate has slipped to 4.4% from 5.7%.
